extraction.document_summary: AIA Elite HomeCare is a home insurance plan (with building and household contents cover) that also extends protection to certain events worldwide when you travel. It is described as a “first-loss policy”, so the brochure states AIA will compensate accordingly if the home is not insured for its full value. Cover is offered in three named tiers: Standard, Comprehensive, and Executive. For example, Building coverage is S$80,000 (Standard), S$120,000 (Comprehensive) and S$260,000 (Executive), while Contents coverage is S$16,000 / S$24,000 / S$37,000. The plan also provides worldwide personal liability up to S$500,000 across all tiers, and Worldwide Accidental Death benefit of S$20,000 (with Double Indemnity for Accidental Death of S$40,000 for certain causes within the building). Worldwide medical reimbursement for accidents is shown as S$250 across tiers, and a “5-Year Premium Waiver” is indicated as “Yes” for all tiers if Death/TPD occurs.
quality_notes: The brochure provides a clear tier table for Standard/Comprehensive/Executive with many specific benefit limits and sub-limits.
Some benefit-limit values are embedded in fragmented table formatting; nonetheless, the numeric amounts and tier mapping are mostly explicit.
Eligibility for the medical reimbursement/accidental death benefit is explicitly described as age-based for the insured and spouse/legal child.

policies.quick_summary: Home insurance with building and contents coverage, extended worldwide items/accidents/travel-related benefits, plus worldwide personal liability, accidental death and medical reimbursement, and a 5-year premium waiver option after Death/Total Permanent Disability. Offered in Standard, Comprehensive, and Executive tiers with different building/contents limits and an indicated annual premium per tier (inclusive of 9% GST). Described as a first-loss policy with compensation adjusted for underinsurance (no penalty for underinsurance). Deductibles apply on most claims except specified categories (e.g., fire and certain accident benefits).
coverage_scope: Building (property insured) and specified extensions (e.g., accidental breakage of fixed glass other than principal perils)
Household contents and personal property against insured Principal Perils
Worldwide unscheduled/scheduled personal valuables for specified categories

Worldwide accidental death and double indemnity for accidental death (within the building, for certain causes)
Accidental breakage/other specified incidents (e.g., replacement of locks and keys due to Principal Perils, credit card/ATM misuse due to loss or theft)
Travel-related items (e.g., travelling baggage; payment in excess of airline compensation)

policies.eligibility_notes: Worldwide Medical Reimbursement for Accidents and Worldwide Accidental Death benefit eligibility is limited by age and student status as stated.
important_caveats: First-loss policy: compensation is adjusted if you do not insure the home for its full value (no penalty for underinsurance).

Deductible applies on all claims except for specific categories listed (e.g., fire; Worldwide Accident Medical Reimbursement; Worldwide Accidental Death Benefit; Double Indemnity for Accidental Death Benefit).
The brochure states there are exclusions such as deliberate/wilful act, negligence, and self-destruction where no benefits will be payable (full list in policy contract).

source_evidence.quote: AIA Elite HomeCare is more than your average home insurance plan.
With four tiers of protection to choose from, the plan can be tailored to your unique needs.
In addition, this is a first-loss policy, so if you choose not to insure your home for its full value, we will compensate you accordingly, with no penalty for underinsurance.

There is a deductible of S$100 or 5%, whichever is higher, of the claim amount on all claims except for loss or damage due to fire, Worldwide Accident Medical Reimbursement, Worldwide Accidental Death Benefit and Double Indemnity for Accidental Death Benefit.

review_notes: The brochure mentions four tiers, but the benefits table shown lists Standard/Comprehensive/Executive; no explicit fourth tier name/amount is present in the provided Markdown.
Some numeric rows appear fragmented (e.g., loss of rent line). Where mapping was ambiguous, numeric extraction confidence is set to medium/low.
